30e08021f9.q: Why do most divorce cases not require attorneys to exchange the same documents twice during financial discovery?
30e08021f9.a: Catherine and Shalhoub argue that in most cases, spouses will voluntarily provide information when given the opportunity and benefit of the doubt. Only a small percentage of people refuse to give information, and those are the cases that end up going to trial. The redundancy of having two attorneys collect the same documents is inefficient, yet remains standard practice in family law.

cd3ddeaf74.q: What is the difference between an amicable divorce and being financially informed in divorce?
cd3ddeaf74.a: Amicable means staying out of court and not fighting, but does not automatically mean you are financially informed. One party may say 'I will take care of you' without providing supporting documentation or helping you understand what assets and debts are actually divided. Being financially informed requires documented knowledge of what you are receiving and what it means for your post-divorce life, even if the process remains amicable.

36c17d819d.q: How can small legal details in a divorce agreement create major financial problems years later?
36c17d819d.a: Catherine's personal example: she remained on the deed of the marital home after divorce but never forced her ex-spouse to refinance or remove her name. When he later became angry and threatened to sue her over an unrelated matter, she discovered she was still legally liable for the house and any mortgage debt, despite being financially stable at signing. Details about property transfers, business ownership, and post-divorce responsibilities must be addressed immediately, not deferred.
